name: Soursop leaf tea
what_people_do: Steep soursop (graviola) leaves, or eat or juice the fruit, for sleep, nerves, "sugar", and increasingly as a cancer remedy.
why_they_say_it_works: Said to calm the nerves and, in recent social media, to kill cancer cells.

documented_by.source: Mahabir D, Gulliford MC 1997, Rev Panam Salud Publica, PMID 9128111
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Among 622 Trinidad diabetes patients, soursop was one of the plants preferentially used for non-diabetes indications.

documented_by.source: Lannuzel A et al 2008, Mov Disord, PMID 18816693
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Guadeloupe: atypical parkinsonism makes up about two thirds of parkinsonism on the island; the fruit toxin annonacin is proposed as a cause (practice of eating soursop is the exposure being studied).

evidence.population: Laboratory and animal; no human trials found
evidence.finding: MSK: human studies are lacking; no proof of benefit for cancer patients; alkaloids caused movement disorders in vitro.
Associational: heavy consumption linked with atypical parkinsonism; causation not proven.

source.name: Lannuzel A et al 2008, Mov Disord, PMID 18816693

harm_note: Neurotoxicity signal from the Guadeloupe work (associational) and no human evidence of cancer benefit. Soursop as a cancer treatment is a harm practice in the bank rules.
gaps: Dose-response for regular leaf tea not established.
Mahabir figure for soursop use is a rank, not a prevalence.
